subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking profile + quantization regression checks
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@skyward.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff — performance benchmarking scope and close milestones

Alex — thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our MAP discussion I’m putting the performance/eval scope and a proposed close timeline in one place so we have a single source of truth for open items. Short summary:

- Objective: Validate Redwood Dedicated configuration for Skyward production workload at target TTFT <= 120ms,  p50 token latency <= 45ms, sustained throughput 1100 tokens/sec at 16 concurrent sessions (chat-style concurrency), and no regressions vs baseline FP16/BF16 when we enable INT8/INT4.
- Deliverables by Redwood: benchmark results (latency/throughput/TTFT/concurrency), kernel profile per quantization mode, regression checklist, and an action plan for any regression (rollback/canary).
- Proposed milestones:
  1) 2027-04-12 — baseline FP16/BF16 run; perf report + raw traces.
  2) 2027-04-15 — INT8 runs + kernel profile export.
  3) 2027-04-18 — INT4 exploratory run; regression analysis.
  4) 2027-04-20 — MAP update + decision point for canary.
  5) 2027-04-27 — planned canary rollout (if agreed).

I’ve attached the initial benchmarking templates (map-milestones-ttft-concurrency.xlsx). Marissa and Karthik will run the full suite and share results; Soojin will coordinate the observability hooks you requested.

Action items for you: confirm the TTFT target above (<= 120ms) and whether we should include a hard SLA requirement for 99th percentile latency in the MAP. If you want, we can instrument the client SDK to capture TTFT and report token-level latencies back to your dashboard during canary.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@skyward.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@skyward.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance benchmarking scope and close milestones

Thanks Sean — quick clarifying questions before the runs:

- TTFT: we can accept <=120ms for initial canary, but for GA we prefer <=100ms. Will Redwood include both thresholds in the MAP?
- Concurrency: 16 sessions is our baseline, but our peak is 24 concurrent sessions during business hours. Can you run a 24-concurrency stress test and include both 16 and 24 in the report?
- Regression tolerance: we need to set a guardrail: no more than +5% p50 latency and no more than +10% 99th percentile when moving to INT8. Is that acceptable?

Also looped in procurement to surface timing constraints on contract redlines — we need benchmark artifacts attached for legal to sign off.

—Alex
Head of ML Engineering — Skyward AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@skyward.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: FP16/BF16 baseline + INT8 initial results (attached)

Alex — attached are the baseline and initial INT8 summary PDFs and the kernel profile CSV. High-level notes:

- Environment: Dedicated pool (A100s, 80GB), model: open-gptx-34B-v2 (baseline FP16/BF16), sequence length 1024 (median 256), prompt distributions from Skyward test set.
- FP16 baseline (p50 token latency): 42ms; p95 token latency: 110ms; TTFT median: 88ms; sustained throughput 1250 tokens/sec at 16 sessions; at 24 sessions throughput drops to 1180 tokens/sec with p95 tail increase.
- INT8 (quantization with per-channel calibration): p50 token latency improved to 37ms; p95 token latency 115ms (tail slightly worse in some cases); TTFT median: 95ms. Throughput: 1350 tokens/sec at 16 sessions, 1285 tokens/sec at 24 sessions.
- Kernel profile: we see hot path shifts to int8_matmul_v3 and changed memory patterns — CSV lists kernels and cumulative time. Notable kernel: int8_matmul_v3_k7 shows increased variance under 24-session load.
- Regression flags: although p50 improved for INT8, TTFT increased for some cold-start prompts (95ms vs 88ms). We believe this is due to calibration and extra pre-processing in the INT8 codepath (per-request quantization checks).

Attachments: skyward_map_bench_results_v1.pdf, kernel_profiles_int8_vs_fp16.csv

Next steps we propose: INT4 exploratory run (we expect more variance), and a focused optimization pass to reduce TTFT penalties in int8 pre-processing (estimated 3-4 business days).

- Marissa
Senior Perf Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@skyward.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: INT4 exploratory run + regression analysis notes

Alex/Team — ran the INT4 exploratory profile (per-layer symmetric quant + minmax fallback). Key observations and mitigations below.

Summary metrics (median values across 10 runs):
- FP16 baseline: p50 token latency = 42ms; TTFT median = 88ms; sustained throughput (16 sessions) = 1250 tok/s.
- INT8: p50 = 37ms; TTFT median = 95ms; throughput (16) = 1350 tok/s.
- INT4 (exploratory): p50 = 33ms; TTFT median = 130ms; throughput (16) = 1480 tok/s.

Analysis:
- INT4 improves raw token throughput and p50 latency but introduces significant TTFT overhead (median +42ms) and large tail variance (p99 increases ~35% in some prompt shapes). This matches expectations — per-request dequant and per-layer fallback checks add work before first token.
- Kernel-level: identified int4_matmul_k2 and dequant_dispatch_k1 as top contributors to TTFT. The kernel CSV rows: int4_matmul_k2 (avg 12.8ms per call), dequant_dispatch_k1 (avg 18.4ms). Several kernels show non-linear scaling at 24 concurrency — causing the p95/p99 tails to blow up.
- Regression policy: given Skyward's guardrail (+5% p50, +10% p99), INT8 passes p50 (improves) but fails the p99 in certain workloads. INT4 fails both TTFT and p99 criteria in current implementation.

Proposed remediation plan:
1) Fast path optimization for INT8: remove redundant per-request calibration for pinned models; implement shared calibration cache (ETA: 3 business days) — owner: Karthik.
2) Canary config: start canary with INT8 + shared calibration cache limited to 10% of traffic; monitor TTFT and p99 for 48 hours — owner: Marissa.
3) INT4: keep exploratory, not for canary until kernel-level dequant path is optimized; include as a future performance option.

We’ll document the kernel IDs and traces in the CSV and provide suggested build flags for the runtime to reduce dequant overhead.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procure@skyward.ai>

Thanks for the artifacts. Legal will need the FP16 baseline + INT8 perf artifacts attached to the procurement packet. We are OK to accept the INT8 canary with the remediation plan you outlined as part of the contract, assuming the canary timeline and rollback are documented in the MAP.

Please confirm: canary start target 2027-04-27, 10% traffic, 48 hrs monitoring window, immediate rollback to FP16 if p99 > baseline +10% or TTFT exceeds 120ms for >1% of requests.

- Procurement — Skyward AI

Subject: MAP update — agreed canary & next steps

All — confirming the MAP update and next steps per today’s thread:

Agreed canary terms (added to MAP doc / HubSpot):
- Canary start: 2027-04-27; traffic: 10% (gradually ramp to 10% over 30 mins).
- Monitoring window: 48 hours with automated rollback triggers: p99 > baseline +10% OR TTFT > 120ms for >1% of requests.
- Owner matrix: Karthik (INT8 calibration cache), Marissa (observability + runbook), Sean (contract & decision).
- Deliverables before canary: updated kernel_profiles_int8_vs_fp16.csv (with flagged kernel IDs), skyward_map_bench_results_v1.pdf (with 16/24 concurrency breakdown), and the MAP milestone spreadsheet.

Open items:
- Marissa to deliver the optimized INT8 calibration cache build by 2027-04-25.
- Marissa/Karthik to run a 24-concurrency verification on 2027-04-24 and share traces.
- Skyward to confirm the GA TTFT target (<=100ms) by 2027-04-26; if GA target is tightened we will outline additional perf work and re-run the MAP.

I’ll update HubSpot and attach the procurement-ready artifacts this afternoon.

Thanks everyone — on track for canary next week.
Sean
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
